payoff: 'So the motor spins 15.0x for each turn of the engine' is wrong for this starter. The Saab WIS gives a Bosch DW 12V 0 001 108 080, and DW is Bosch's permanent-magnet starter with a planetary reduction gear (see the Bosch starter poster; MAHLE's brochure also says most modern starters drive through a reduction gear). So the armature turns several times per pinion turn. 135/9 = 15 is the pinion's turns per engine turn, not the motor's. Say 'the pinion spins 15 times for each turn of the engine' (or 'the motor at least 15 times; a gear inside multiplies it again'), and make the payoff picture's turn counter sit on the pinion, not the motor case. The topic's verify list also asks for it to be this starter's ratio, not every car's.

release (minor, fix in the same rewrite): the line runs 'once the engine fires... a spring pulls it back'. MAHLE says the return spring pulls the plunger and pinion back when the ignition switch stops feeding the solenoid, i.e. when the key is let go, not because the engine fired. Suggested: '...lets the pinion spin free; let go of the key, and a spring pulls it back.'
style: {gear_ratio} renders '15.0x' and is spoken 'fifteen point zero times'. Use a whole-number placeholder so it reads 'fifteen times'.
